violations_found.violations:
- Organizational Constraint violated: The EU launches the Sovereign Evaluation Authority, a new body under ENISA and the AI Office, implying immediate organizational creation and operational capacity. However, constitutional constraint #6 ("No measure is implemented instantly") requires a minimum of one full turn for low-cost measures and two for high-cost ones before full effect. The narrative does not describe phased implementation or delayed effect; instead, it presents the authority as active and legally fast-tracked immediately, violating the minimum time lag for implementation.
- Modelling choice violated: The narrative states "Three large measures and a priority strain the agenda," but constitutional constraint #5 limits the EU to at most one new measure per turn. Introducing the Sovereign Evaluation Authority as a new measure while already carrying multiple active measures (including the Frontier Access Guarantee and Labour Transition Accelerator Fund) and implying it begins legal fast-tracking and operational design in the same turn violates the "at most one new measure per turn" rule. The notepad lists the Sovereign Evaluation Authority as a new entry with a portfolio charge, confirming it is treated as a new measure introduced this turn—this is a second new measure at minimum (if not more), which is not permitted.
